steps.title: The complete record
steps.body: Every mention, assignment, and unblock. Slack DMs can be missed or muted; this list never loses one.

steps.title: Open your preferences
steps.body: This is the screen worth spending two minutes on today rather than on the day it annoys you.

steps.title: Per-category, per-channel
steps.body: Each category can go in-app, to Slack, both, or neither. Tune it here rather than muting Constellation in Slack outright — a member nobody can reach is a member who stops getting asked.

steps.title: Communication lives together
steps.body: Open Social to find channels, members, and the club's shared schedule in one place.

compact.body: Communication lives on this bar: Chat holds every channel you can read, and Calendar sits beside it. The Chat list starts with People & DMs, which is also available under More.

steps.title: Now the calendar
steps.body: Notifications tell you what already happened. The calendar shows the meetings and dates ahead.

steps.title: Meetings and deadlines together
steps.body: Club events, project milestones, and task due dates on one grid. If it isn't here, it isn't happening.

steps.title: RSVP means something
steps.body: Open an event and RSVP. Officers plan around the count — food, room size, whether the meeting happens at all — so a missing RSVP is a real cost, not a formality.

steps.title: Back home
steps.body: One last thing to point at.

compact.body: One last thing to point at. Tap Home.

steps.title: It all lands here
steps.body: Everything you just configured surfaces on this panel. Notifications tell you the moment something changes; this tells you what's coming.

compact.body: Expand the 7-day agenda to see what is coming after the Next event card.

steps.title: And Constellation reads it too
steps.body: These cards are generated from your projects — risks, capacity, things that have gone quiet. Treat them as a colleague's opinion: often useful, occasionally wrong, never the final word.

compact.body: Expand Project insights for risks, capacity, and quiet work. Treat them as useful signals, not the final word.
